headline: Gujarat HC quashes ₹43.43 cr GST demand on Amul federation for non cross-charging
reference: M/s Gujarat Co-operative Milk Marketing Federation Ltd vs Union of India & Ors., R/SCA No. 7085 of 2025, Gujarat High Court, decided 14.10.2026
summary_points: Issue: whether Section 74 CGST Act could be invoked for IGST on HO common expenses and salaries not cross-charged to branches (Jul 2017-Mar 2019).
Held: Order-in-Original dated 01.01.2025 confirming ₹43,43,12,441 IGST with interest and penalty was quashed; Section 74 was invoked mechanically.
Court said SCN and order recorded no foundational facts of fraud, wilful misstatement or suppression; DGGI investigation alone is not enough.
Citing Tata Steel (SC, 2026), court held extended period needs recorded satisfaction; the situation was revenue-neutral as ITC would have been available to registered branches.
Impact: taxpayers can challenge Section 74 demands on internal HO-branch supplies where intent to evade is not specifically shown.
who_is_affected: Multi-branch businesses and HO entities facing GST demands for non cross-charging of internal services, especially under Section 74.
action_required: Review pending Section 73/74 notices on HO-branch supplies for lack of specific allegations of suppression or intent to evade, and consider writ or reply based on this ruling.

social.linkedin:
Gujarat High Court quashes a ₹43.43 crore GST demand against Gujarat Co-operative Milk Marketing Federation (Amul).

The department had treated Head Office and branches as distinct persons under Section 25(4) CGST Act and taxed common expenses and HO salaries not cross-charged to branches for July 2017 to March 2019, invoking Section 74.

The Division Bench held that the adjudicating authority invoked Section 74 mechanically. Neither the show cause notice nor the order recorded foundational facts showing fraud, wilful misstatement or suppression. Relying on the Supreme Court's Tata Steel ruling, the court said these words cannot be recited as a routine formula to bypass normal limitation.

The court also noted that even with cross-charging, the exercise would have been revenue-neutral because ITC would be available to registered branches, and the expenses were fully recorded in the books.

The Order-in-Original dated 01.01.2025 was quashed.

Practical takeaway: Section 74 demands on internal HO-branch services need specific findings on intent to evade.

Please verify with the official judgment before acting on it.
